recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is; no core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6048 unless a future Security work-group decision changes Signature.who target resources.
issue_request: FHIR-6048 is a Published/Persuasive Security change request asking that digital signatures be allowed to reference Device resources; the approved resolution was to add Device to Signature.who as an allowed resource.
initial_application: Commit 7680a21d741140fb7104da32f2a217d2b0b25d2e explicitly referenced #6048 and changed Signature.who[x] from uri|Reference(Practitioner|RelatedPerson|Patient) to uri|Reference(Practitioner|RelatedPerson|Patient|Device|Organization). Later datatype refactors retained Device while changing the shape to Signature.who Reference(...).
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Signature as an active normative datatype in current build scope. Current source/datatypes/signature.xml has Signature.who typed as Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|RelatedPerson|Patient|Device|Organization). Later Signature changes such as FHIR-9533 and FHIR-9563 are separate background issues and do not alter the FHIR-6048 Device allowance. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct or conflicting FHIR-6048 evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current authoritative source already implements the requested Device support for Signature.who.

related_jiras.note: Separate published Contract change to use the Signature datatype; it does not affect whether Signature.who allows Device.
Separate published Signature enhancement adding onBehalfOf; current source uses a matching target-resource family there, but FHIR-6048 only required Signature.who.
